subject: Feature escrow requirement for Globex commitment
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@globex-fin.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Feature escrow requirement for enterprise commitment

Soojin —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Good momentum on our side; legal and procurement are pushing to close by end of month. Before they sign, two items have to be represented in the SOW:

1) A limited feature-escrow mechanism so that if Redwood ever ceases service or is unable to provide a hosted endpoint, Globex can run a pre-packaged inference bundle in our environment for up to 90 days.
2) A runbook and test harness for the on-prem fallback (simple dockerized runtime + inference schema) — Globex security needs to validate black-box behavior with our telemetry.

We attached a short MVP requirements doc (attached). Can you let us know whether this is feasible, and what level of commitment (engineering time / support) would be required? Procurement also asked for a high-level ETA so they can include it in the contract schedule.

Appreciate quick clarity — this is gating our purchase order.

—Ethan

Attachments: Globex_MVP_requirements.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@globex-fin.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature escrow requirement for enterprise commitment

Ethan —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the MVP doc. I looped in Product and Eng to scope effort and confirm feasibility. High-level response for procurement: we can commit to a documented escrow-runbook and a lightweight on-prem inference bundle for a narrow set of verified model artifacts. I need to confirm the engineering ETA and what falls under standard support vs. a paid professional services engagement.

I expect an internal alignment within the day and will share a recommended schedule and SOW language you can present to procurement.

Next step: I will send a short internal brief to our PM and Eng (cc'd) to request prioritization — can you confirm the contractual deadline (PO signed by 2027-06-30) and whether Globex expects the actual fallback package to be delivery-ready at signing or within an agreed delivery window post-sign?

Thanks,
Soojin
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: [Action required] Globex: escrow runbook + on-prem fallback — prioritization ask

Team —

Quick context: Globex (large FS prospect, deal GLOBEX-2027-325) will sign only if we include a narrow "feature escrow" clause: runbook + a lightweight inference bundle (dockerized) they can run for up to 90 days if Redwood is unavailable. Procurement wants an ETA to include in the SOW. Attached is their MVP requirements.

Why this matters: $1.6M ARR initial commitment, strong expansion upside; procurement deadline is 2027-06-30. This is a sales-blocker and likely a one-off legal ask, but it sets precedent for future enterprise customers.

Asks:
- Marissa (PM): can you weigh in on scope (supported models, security constraints, telemetry/stubbed logs) and propose a minimal viable delivery we can commit to in the SOW?
- Ben (Engineering lead): ballpark engineering time (sprint-weeks) to produce a dockerized inference bundle and a test harness + runbook for 1 verified model family. Also flag any compliance/security blockers (KMS, HSM, non-export license concerns).
- Jasmine (Solutions/CS): can you propose a support model (onboarding runbook, verification checklist, optional paid PS) and whether we should offer a 90-day fallback or a shorter validated period?

Constraints to consider: we should avoid committing to full model weights export or broad operational support. Proposal should be conservative — minimal artifacts and clear handoff criteria.

Timeline guidance from me: procurement needs a written ETA for SOW by EOD 2027-06-11 so they can circulate to legal. If we can't provide a deterministic ETA today, we must surface an engagement path (PS scoping call + paid delivery timeline) that gets them comfortable to sign.

Thanks — tagging for visibility: @Marissa @Ben @Jasmine

Attachments: Globex_MVP_requirements.pdf, Globex_ESCROW_SOW_draft.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Action required] Globex: escrow runbook + on-prem fallback — prioritization ask

Thanks for the context. Quick assessment and suggested compromise below.

Scope (MVP we can commit to in SOW):
- Supported artifacts: packaged inference bundle containing a verified, quantized model variant (customer-acknowledged list) + inference container image. No raw weights export.
- Runbook: step-by-step deploy guide, smoke-test harness (curl-based), and verification checklist for accuracy/latency.
- Telemetry: limited black-box telemetry schema (request/response hashes, latency histogram) suitable for Globex to validate behavior; no token-level logs by default.
- Support: 8 business hours of onboarding assistance (remote), and an optional paid PS engagement for additional verification and telemetry integration.

Estimated effort (rough):
- Product scoping and SOW language: 2-3 person-days
- Engineering build (one verified model family, container + harness): 2 x engs for 3 sprints (3 weeks) inclusive of one round of QA in staging.
- Runbook and documentation: 3-4 person-days (tech writer + eng)

Risks and constraints:
- KMS/HSM integration for keys inside customer env is out of scope for MVP. If Globex insists on customer KMS, we need a paid PS + security review.
- Any request to escrow proprietary third-party model weights may require licensing review.

Recommendation for SOW wording (short): "Redwood will provide a verified inference bundle and deployment runbook for a mutually-agreed model variant. Redwood will provide 8 hours of remote onboarding assistance; extended verification and KMS integration are available as paid professional services."

If the customer needs delivery within signing (by 2027-06-30) we cannot guarantee in-house engineering delivery within that window without a paid PS engagement and priority sprint allocation. Proposed path: offer SOW language that commits to providing the artifacts within a 30-day delivery window post-sign with the option to accelerate via PS. This protects us operationally and gives procurement a deterministic schedule.

Happy to sync with Ben if you want a tighter engineering ETA.

—Marissa
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Action required] Globex: escrow runbook + on-prem fallback — prioritization ask

Appreciate the concise scope Marissa. Technical addendum:
- Engineering can produce the container + smoke harness in the timelines above, assuming we target only 1 model family and reuse existing CI/CD components.
- We will need a small sprint allocation (2 engineers x 3 sprints) + 1 QA pass. If sales wants acceleration to deliver before PO, we can offer a paid "accelerate" bucket (estimated cost = ~40 engineer-hours @ our PS rate) to hit the signing deadline.
- No export of raw model weights without licensing confirmation; we must document this in SOW to avoid legal exposure.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Soojin: present Marissa's SOW wording and our recommended 30-day post-sign delivery window (with paid acceleration option) to Globex procurement.
2) If Globex insists on delivery at signing, request a PS scoping call and we'll produce a stamped ETA the same day.

I'll block time for a quick sync if needed.

—Ben
Engineering Lead, Inference Runtime
